name: Amalekites
summary: A nomadic raiding people of the Negev and Sinai, descended from Esau's grandson Amalek. They were the first nation to attack Israel after the Exodus, striking the weary stragglers. Their unending hostility made Amalek the archetype of the enemy of God's people, from Moses' raised hands to Saul's lost kingdom and, by tradition, to Haman in the book of Esther.

origin.account: Timna, concubine of Esau's son Eliphaz, bore him Amalek, who became a duke (chief) of Edom. Genesis 14:7 speaks of 'the country of the Amalekites' in Abraham's day, which most interpreters read as naming the region by its later inhabitants.

lineage.ancestor: Amalek, son of Eliphaz, son of Esau
lineage.notes: Timna, Amalek's mother, was sister of the Horite chief Lotan. So the Amalekites were an Edomite–Horite branch that split off as a separate nomadic nation.

homeland.region: The Negev and northern Sinai — 'the land of the south'
homeland.description: Desert nomads ranging from the Negev south of Judah into Sinai and 'from Havilah until thou comest to Shur, that is over against Egypt'. They moved with camels and flocks and raided settled lands.
homeland.modern_location: Southern Israel (Negev) and the Sinai Peninsula of Egypt.

places.name: Rephidim
places.modern_name: Sinai (probably Wadi Refayid or Wadi Feiran)
places.note: Where Amalek attacked Israel and Moses held up his hands.

places.name: The south (Negev)
places.note: 'The Amalekites dwell in the land of the south'.

places.name: Ziklag
places.modern_name: Probably Khirbet a-Ra'i or Tel Sera'
places.note: David's town, burned by Amalekite raiders.

places.name: Mount Seir
places.note: Where the last Amalekites were destroyed in Hezekiah's day.

timeline.event: Amalek attacks Israel at Rephidim. Israel prevails while Moses' hands are held up; Moses builds an altar, Jehovah-nissi, and God vows war on Amalek 'from generation to generation'.
Israel's unauthorised invasion of Canaan is crushed by the Amalekites and Canaanites at Hormah.
Balaam foretells Amalek's end: 'Amalek was the first of the nations; but his latter end shall be that he perish for ever.'
Amalek joins Moab and later Midian in raiding Israel.
Saul is commanded to destroy Amalek. He spares King Agag and the best livestock, and is told 'to obey is better than sacrifice'. God rejects him as king.
Amalekites burn Ziklag and take David's families captive. David recovers all. An Amalekite claims to have killed Saul and is executed.
Simeonites destroy 'the rest of the Amalekites that were escaped' at Mount Seir — the last historical mention.
Haman 'the Agagite' plots to destroy all Jews; Jewish tradition makes him a descendant of Agag the Amalekite.

religion.practices: Scripture records nothing of their gods. It judges them for their conduct: they 'feared not God' and preyed on the weak.

importance: Amalek stands for unprovoked cruelty against the weak and for opposition to God's purpose. They struck the faint stragglers at the rear, and Israel was commanded, 'Remember what Amalek did unto thee.' The battle at Rephidim is the Bible's first picture of intercession: victory came as Moses' hands were held up. Saul's failure against Amalek shows that partial obedience is disobedience, and it cost him his throne. In Esther the old conflict returns in Haman the Agagite.

impact.how: The first battle after the Exodus; Joshua's first command and Moses' first recorded memorial.
Sparing Agag cost him the kingdom.
At Ziklag, facing loss and mutiny, he 'encouraged himself in the LORD his God'.

impact.who: Mordecai, Esther and the Jews of Persia
impact.how: Haman's genocide plot was overturned; the feast of Purim remembers it.

notable_people.name: Agag
notable_people.role: King spared by Saul and killed by Samuel

notable_people.name: Haman the Agagite
notable_people.role: Enemy of the Jews in Esther (tradition links him to Agag)

key_verses.text: And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed: and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.
For he said, Because the LORD hath sworn that the LORD will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.

Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come forth out of Egypt; How he met thee by the way, and smote the hindmost of thee, even all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary; and he feared not God. Therefore it shall be, when the LORD thy God hath given thee rest from all thine enemies round about, in the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee for an inheritance to possess it, that thou shalt blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven; thou shalt not forget it.
And Samuel said, Hath the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.

fate.summary: The last Amalekite remnant was destroyed by the tribe of Simeon at Mount Seir in Hezekiah's reign. After that the Bible knows them only through Haman's title 'the Agagite'.

today.summary: No Amalekites exist today, and they are not identified in any known inscription outside the Bible. In Jewish tradition 'Amalek' is the symbol of irrational hatred of God's people. Deuteronomy 25:17-19 is read in synagogues on Shabbat Zachor, the sabbath before Purim.
today.modern_legacy: The symbol of Amalek and the Purim festival.
